name: Silimo
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.quote: De duidelijkheid van hun spreken laat weinig te wenschen over, en werd ook 't door ons teruggegeven woord nagenoeg altijd onmiddellijk herkend, waarbij het van groot voordeel was, dat de klemtoon steeds op de laatste lettergreep der woorden valt. [voetnoot 1:] Een uitzondering maakt het woord „halëbok" met den klemtoon op de eerste lettergreep tenzij „ha" als een afzonderlijk woord moet worden opgevat.
new_statements.translation: The clarity of their speech leaves little to be desired, and a word we repeated back to them was almost always recognised immediately, in which it was a great advantage that the stress always falls on the last syllable of words. [footnote 1:] An exception is the word 'halëbok' [a greeting], with the stress on the first syllable, unless 'ha' is to be taken as a separate word.
new_statements.citation: van Nouhuys, J. W. 1912. Eerste bijdrage tot de kennis van de taal der „Pësëgem" van Centraal Nieuw-Guinea, verzameld tijdens de Expeditie 1909/1910 naar het Sneeuwgebergte. Bijdragen tot de Taal-, Land- en Volkenkunde van Nederlandsch-Indië 66: 266-273. DOI 10.1163/22134379-90001817
new_statements.locator: p. 267, main text and footnote 1 (p. 2 of the saved extract; Delpher BKI 1912 (66) volgno 3, p. 265)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: QUOTE: Opened (8 pages = printed pp. 266-273; extracted text copy..) and the page scan printed p. 267). The passage is there verbatim: "De duidelijkheid van hun spreken laat weinig te wenschen over, en werd ook 't door ons teruggegeven woord nagenoeg altijd onmiddellijk herkend, waarbij het van groot voordeel was, dat de klemtoon steeds op de laatste lettergreep der woorden valt.¹" and footnote 1: "Een uitzondering maakt het woord „halëbok" met den klemtoon op de eerste lettergreep tenzij „ha" als een afzonderlijk woord moet worden opgevat." (the compiler "[voetnoot 1:]" is an editorial label, not print.) DOI 10.1163/22134379-90001817 matches the saved CrossRef record (: BKI 66: 266-273, 19…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is always on the final syllable (fixed final), as observed by the expedition's naval officer during first contact; a single lexical exception is noted (halëbok, first-syllable stress, possibly a two-word phrase ha + lëbok).
new_statements.exceptions: halëbok 'greeting' stressed on the first syllable, unless 'ha' is a separate word.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level, elicited isolated citation forms from a c. 150-item first-contact wordlist (29 Oct 1909 onward); the list itself hyphenates syllables but does not mark stress. Author was a naval officer, not a linguist. The language is that of the 'Pësëgem' of the upper Lorentz (Noord) River valley between the Treub and Wichmann ranges (c. 4°28'S 138°43'E, 1500-1700 m); see the note on which variety for the Silimo-vs-Nduga assignment problem.
new_statements.identity_note: The statement is for the 'Pësëgem' (Pesegem, Pesechem) language met by the Lorentz expedition 1909-10 in the upper Lorentz (Noord) River valley between the Treub and Wichmann ranges (c. 4°28'S 138°43'E), not for a variety called Silimo. Its assignment is contested: Bromley 1981: 3-4 ('South Ngalik, including the language of the Pesegem') and Voorhoeve 1975: 37 (no. 65 'SOUTH NGALIK (Pesechem)') equate it with South Ngalik = Silimo [wul] sili1249; Glottolog 5.1 (language code tags on van Nouhuys 1915, Snell, Fischer 1915, van den Broek 1915, de Bruijn 1941: 'Pesechem = Nduga [ndx]'), Carrington 1996 (Pesechem indexed under Nduga) and Pawley & Hammarström 2018: 41 (van Nouhuys 1912 and Le Roux 1950: 901-913 listed under Nduga) assign it to Nduga [ndx] ndug1245. The Pesegem site lies roughly midway between the Glottolog points for Silimo (-4.53, 139.00) and Nduga (-4.34, 138.41). A curator must decide whether this 1912 fixed: final syllable observation is filed under sili1249, ndug1245, or both with a cross-reference; no stress statement exists for Silimo under that name.

readall_conflicts: The standing issue is one of identity rather than placement: the only first-hand stress statement for this item, van Nouhuys 1912 (BKI 66: 267; 'de klemtoon steeds op de laatste lettergreep der woorden valt', exception halebok with initial stress), describes the 'Pesegem' of the upper Lorentz valley, which Bromley 1981: 3-4 and Voorhoeve 1975: 37 assign to South Ngalik = Silimo, but which Glottolog 5.1, Carrington 1996 and Pawley & Hammarstrom 2018: 41 assign to Nduga [ndx] (ndug1245). The final-stress reading is therefore secure for the Pesegem data but its attachment to Silimo rather than Nduga is contested.
